result.title: AdvMTO: Multimodal and Temporal Adversarial Object Attacks via 2D Gaussian Splatting for BEV-Based 3D Object Detection
result.summary: Adversarial object attacks pose a threat to BEV-based 3D object detectors in autonomous driving. Existing attacks typically target a single modality, coordinate camera and LiDAR observations at the current timestamp, or model temporal persistence mainly in camera streams. Without a unified construction of current and historical observations, attacks can leave part of the detector's accumulated evidence unsuppressed, limiting their effectiveness. In this paper, we propose AdvMTO, a 2D Gaussian Splatting (2DGS) framework for suppressing detection of persistent adversarial objects. Its oriented surfels encode appearance, geometry, and opacity in one object state, from which camera images and scanline LiDAR returns are generated. AdvMTO then constructs current and historical inputs through detector-native processing, regenerating LiDAR returns in each native source sweep for fusion detectors. We optimize bounded appearance perturbations for each detector, propagating gradients through historical BEV memory for temporal camera detectors. For fusion detectors, bounded geometry refinement along local normals further perturbs both sensing modalities. Experiments on nuScenes demonstrate effective suppression of traffic-cone detection across three BEV detectors. Temporal ablations further highlight the importance of detector-native history modeling for both attack construction and optimization.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 AdvMTO，用 2D Gaussian Splatting 的定向 surfel 统一编码外观、几何与不透明度，生成相机与 LiDAR 观测，并构造当前与历史输入、沿历史 BEV 记忆回传梯度，以抑制 BEV 3D 检测器对持久对抗物体的检测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「扰动历史记忆中被累积保留的视觉证据以抑制检测」可作为一种探针思路，供核查 latent 状态里视觉证据的留存与因果作用；但论文对象是 BEV 3D 检测而非 VLM 推理，与主线距离较远。
